historical_probe_conclusions: Three core splits produce 23 C++ LTCG records; all seven produce 27. Matching that count does not establish the original partitions or filenames.
Both combined experiments preserve the entire readonly, writable and resource sections byte for byte, and all 1,381 common code/data public addresses.

Tracking alone and emitter alone preserve every code byte. COP1 alone or both tracking/emitter together change 12 code bytes in WritePhysicalWord. All seven splits change 8 bytes in that same previously unmatched function.

The changed bytes are operand evaluation/register choices for additions; no moved addresses or relocations explain them. This demonstrates cross-unit LTCG context sensitivity and does not prove an improved original-image match.
All other native function bodies, including Branch, ResetCPU and CompareBrowserItems, remain identical to their pinned baseline bodies. No claim is made about later source revisions.
All literal/asset/float placements stay unchanged; the generated 4294967296.0f constant remains at 43E04C instead of target 43E01C.
No partition is promoted solely to reproduce the Rich contribution count. Original file organization remains non-unique.
